plates.side_label: 300,000 PEOPLE ON SAME STREETS: SOUTHWARK (1,263 DEATHS / 40,046 HOUSES) VS LAMBETH (98 / 26,107)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked street-pipe and mortality comparison diagram from John Snow (1855, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera) shows intermingled Southwark & Vauxhall pipes (sewage-tainted Thames at Battersea: 1,263 deaths in 40,046 houses = 315 per 10,000) vs Lambeth Company pipes (clean Thames Ditton intake: 98 deaths in 26,107 houses = 37 per 10,000).

teach_overlay.label: 300,000 SOUTH LONDONERS: SOUTHWARK PIPE (315/10,000 DEATHS) VS LAMBETH PIPE (37/10,000 DEATHS)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked street-pipe & mortality comparison diagram on period paper from John Snow (1855, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera) showing intermingled Southwark & Vauxhall pipes (sewage-tainted Thames at Battersea: 1,263 deaths in 40,046 houses = 315 per 10,000) vs Lambeth Company pipes (clean Thames Ditton intake: 98 deaths in 26,107 houses = 37 per 10,000)
teach_overlay.scale: three hundred thousand Londoners living side by side on the exact same streets unwittingly took part in a blind medical trial — and the dirty pipe killed more than eight times as many neighbours as the clean one
